cards.name: Siddhartha (The Prince)
fact_file: Born in Lumbini as heir to the Sakya clan
Raised in luxury, shielded from suffering
Mastered martial arts and scholarly pursuits
cards.famous_story: Left palace at 29 after seeing the Four Sights: old age, sickness, death, and a wandering ascetic.

cards.name: King Suddhodana
fact_file: King of the Sakya clan in Kapilavastu
Father of Siddhartha Gautama
Tried to prevent his son from becoming an ascetic
cards.famous_story: Built three palaces to keep Siddhartha content, but ultimately could not prevent his son's spiritual quest.

cards.name: Queen Maya
fact_file: Mother of Siddhartha Gautama
Dreamed of a white elephant before his birth
Died seven days after giving birth
cards.famous_story: Her dream of the white elephant entering her womb foretold the birth of a great being who would become Buddha.

cards.name: Mahapajapati Gotami
fact_file: Queen Maya's sister and co-wife of Suddhodana
Raised Siddhartha after Maya's death
First woman ordained as a bhikkhuni (nun)
cards.famous_story: After Buddha's initial refusal, Ananda interceded and she became leader of the first bhikkhuni sangha.

cards.name: Yasodhara (Princess Pimpa)
fact_file: Princess and wife of Siddhartha
Mother of Rahula
Later became an arahant bhikkhuni
cards.famous_story: When Siddhartha left, she cut her hair and wore simple robes, living as if ordained before formal ordination existed.

cards.name: Rahula
fact_file: Buddha's only son, ordained at age 7
Foremost disciple in desire for training
Became arahant as a young man
cards.famous_story: Trained intensively from childhood, mastering discipline and becoming an arahant through dedication to the practice.

cards.name: Devadatta
fact_file: Cousin of Siddhartha, brother of Ananda
Initially a disciple, later became Buddha's rival
Attempted to kill Buddha and split the Sangha
cards.famous_story: Released a maddened elephant to kill Buddha, but the elephant bowed before the Awakened One instead.

cards.name: Nanda
fact_file: Half-brother of Siddhartha
Reluctantly ordained on his wedding day
Eventually became an arahant
cards.famous_story: Buddha showed him celestial nymphs to overcome his attachment, then taught him true renunciation of all desire.

cards.name: The Five Ascetics
fact_file: First five disciples of Buddha
Practiced extreme asceticism with Siddhartha
Received the first sermon at Deer Park
cards.famous_story: Initially dismissed Buddha for ending his ascetic practices, but became the first arahants after hearing the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta.

cards.name: Sariputta
fact_file: Chief disciple, foremost in wisdom
Former wandering ascetic and philosopher
Attained arahantship within days of ordination
cards.famous_story: Converted after hearing Assaji recite one verse; became Buddha's 'right-hand' disciple and greatest teacher after Buddha himself.

cards.name: Maha Moggallana
fact_file: Chief disciple, foremost in psychic powers
Childhood friend of Sariputta
Could travel to celestial and hell realms
cards.famous_story: Used his psychic powers to shake Indra's palace to dispel the god's pride, demonstrating the supremacy of spiritual attainment.

cards.name: Maha Kassapa
fact_file: Foremost in ascetic practices (dhutanga)
Presided over the First Buddhist Council
Received Buddha's robe, becoming the first patriarch
cards.famous_story: Buddha once offered to exchange robes with him, signifying Kassapa as his successor in maintaining strict discipline.

cards.name: Ananda
fact_file: Buddha's personal attendant for 25 years
Foremost in hearing the teachings
Recited all suttas at the First Council
cards.famous_story: Memorized every teaching Buddha gave and recited them at the First Council beginning with 'Thus have I heard...'

cards.name: Anuruddha
fact_file: Cousin of Buddha
Foremost in divine eye (clairvoyance)
Became blind but gained supreme psychic vision
cards.famous_story: After falling asleep during a teaching, vowed never to sleep again; went blind from strain but developed the divine eye.

cards.name: Channa
fact_file: Siddhartha's charioteer during the Four Sights
Accompanied him when he left the palace
Initially arrogant, later reformed and became arahant
cards.famous_story: Drove the chariot on the night Siddhartha renounced the world, holding the horse's hooves so they made no sound.

cards.name: Upali
fact_file: Former barber, lowest caste
Foremost in knowledge of Vinaya (monastic rules)
Recited all Vinaya rules at the First Council
cards.famous_story: Ordained before Sakyan princes to teach humility; became the greatest authority on monastic discipline despite humble origins.

cards.name: Angulimala
fact_file: Former serial killer who wore a garland of fingers
Converted by Buddha despite killing 999 people
Became arahant and symbol of redemption
cards.famous_story: Chased Buddha to kill him for his 1,000th victim but couldn't catch him, leading to his conversion and complete transformation.

cards.name: Khema
fact_file: Former queen, renowned for her beauty
Foremost bhikkhuni in wisdom
Chief female disciple alongside Uppalavanna
cards.famous_story: Buddha used magic to show her an aging celestial nymph, teaching impermanence and leading to her awakening.

cards.name: Uppalavanna
fact_file: Foremost bhikkhuni in psychic powers
Former courtesan of extraordinary beauty
Chief female disciple alongside Khema
cards.famous_story: Attained arahantship while meditating on a lotus, her name meaning 'color of a blue lotus.'

cards.name: Visakha
fact_file: Foremost female lay disciple and benefactor
Extremely wealthy merchant's daughter
Built numerous monasteries and supported sangha
cards.famous_story: Donated the Pubbarama monastery and was granted eight boons by Buddha for her lifelong generosity to the sangha.

cards.name: Queen Mallika
fact_file: Queen of Kosala, wife of King Pasenadi
Known for her wisdom and devotion
Skillfully guided her husband toward Dhamma
cards.famous_story: When her husband blamed her unfairly, she took responsibility to maintain peace, demonstrating perfect patience and wisdom.

cards.name: King Bimbisara of Magadha
fact_file: First royal patron of Buddha
Donated the Bamboo Grove monastery
Powerful ruler of Magadha kingdom
cards.famous_story: Met Buddha before enlightenment and asked him to return after achieving his goal; became Buddha's first royal supporter.

cards.name: King Pasenadi of Kosala
fact_file: King of Kosala, contemporary of Buddha
Close friend and devoted follower
Had many conversations with Buddha recorded in suttas
cards.famous_story: Once came to Buddha dusty from travel, showing his humility and eagerness to receive teachings despite royal status.

cards.name: Anathapindika
fact_file: Wealthy merchant, foremost in generosity
Purchased Jetavana grove for Buddha
Name means 'feeder of the destitute'
cards.famous_story: Covered the ground with gold coins to purchase Jetavana, creating Buddha's most famous monastery.

cards.name: Mara & His Retinue
fact_file: The tempter, embodiment of death and desire
Rules the realm of sensual pleasure
Attempted to prevent Buddha's enlightenment
cards.famous_story: Attacked Buddha under the Bodhi tree with armies and temptations, but Buddha remained unmoved, touching the earth as witness.

cards.name: Mara's Daughters (Tanha, Arati, Raga)
fact_file: Craving, Discontent, and Lust personified
Sent by Mara to tempt Buddha after enlightenment
Transformed into old women to teach impermanence
cards.famous_story: Tried to seduce Buddha with various forms, but he transformed them into crones, teaching them about impermanence.

cards.name: Mara's Army
fact_file: Demonic forces representing mental defilements
Attacked Buddha on the night of enlightenment
Represent internal obstacles to awakening
cards.famous_story: Hurled weapons that became flowers, unleashed storms that became gentle breezes when they approached Buddha's peace.

cards.name: Mucalinda Naga
fact_file: Serpent king who protected Buddha
Sheltered Buddha from storm during meditation
Coiled seven times and spread his hood as umbrella
cards.famous_story: During a great storm in Buddha's fifth week after enlightenment, coiled around him seven times and shielded him with his hood.

cards.name: Naga Kings
fact_file: Powerful serpent deities of lakes and rivers
Some became devoted followers of Buddha
Represent primal forces of nature
cards.famous_story: Various Naga kings listened to Buddha's teachings and became protectors of the Dhamma in their realms.

cards.name: Sakka (Indra)
fact_file: King of the Thirty-Three Gods
Previously a human who became a deity through merit
Frequent visitor and supporter of Buddha
cards.famous_story: Descended from Tavatimsa heaven multiple times to hear teachings and asked Buddha to teach his mother in heaven.

cards.name: Four Great Kings
fact_file: Guardian deities of the four cardinal directions
Protect the world and Buddha's teachings
Rule over various classes of nature spirits
cards.famous_story: Offered Buddha four bowls after his enlightenment, which he miraculously combined into one.

cards.name: Maha Brahma Sahampati
fact_file: Great Brahma deity, ruler of a heaven realm
Convinced Buddha to teach after enlightenment
Represents highest worldly attainment
cards.famous_story: Descended and begged Buddha three times to teach, saying 'there are beings with little dust in their eyes.'

cards.name: Vessantara
fact_file: Buddha's previous life as a prince of perfect generosity
Gave away everything, including his children
Last human birth before becoming Buddha
cards.famous_story: Gave away his magical rain-bringing elephant, his children to a brahmin, and his wife, perfecting the virtue of giving.

cards.name: Buddha
fact_file: Fully awakened one who discovered the Middle Way
Founded Buddhism and taught for 45 years
Achieved complete liberation from suffering
cards.famous_story: Attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree after defeating Mara, becoming the Awakened One who shows the path to Nibbana.

cards.name: Añña Kondañña
fact_file: First person to become arahant after Buddha
Eldest of the Five Ascetics
Declared 'Añña' (Knowledge) at enlightenment
cards.famous_story: Upon hearing Buddha's first sermon, he attained stream-entry. Shortly after, became the first arahant, declaring 'I understand!'

cards.name: Kisa Gotami
fact_file: Lost her only child and was driven to madness by grief
Buddha taught her about impermanence through mustard seed parable
Became an arahant and foremost in wearing coarse robes
cards.famous_story: Seeking to revive her dead child, Buddha sent her to find mustard seeds from a house untouched by death. Finding none, she understood the universality of suffering and impermanence.

cards.name: Emperor Ashoka
fact_file: Unified most of India under Maurya Empire
Converted to Buddhism after bloody Kalinga War
Erected pillars with Buddhist teachings across empire
cards.famous_story: After witnessing the carnage of the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and dedicated his reign to spreading the Dharma through edicts, pillars, and humanitarian works.

cards.name: Sujata
fact_file: Village girl who offered milk rice to starving Siddhartha
Her offering saved him from death by asceticism
Enabled the Middle Way and Buddha's enlightenment
cards.famous_story: Seeing the emaciated ascetic near death, Sujata offered nourishing milk rice. This simple act of compassion saved his life and led him to discover the Middle Way.

cards.name: Amrapali
fact_file: Renowned courtesan of Vesali, known for beauty and wealth
Offered her mango grove to Buddha and the Sangha
Became a nun and attained enlightenment
cards.famous_story: Despite her life of luxury and sensual pleasure, Amrapali recognized the emptiness of worldly pursuits. She ordained as a nun and achieved arahantship.

cards.name: Devaputra Mara
fact_file: Divine form of Mara, god of death and desire
Rules over the realm of sensual pleasure
Tempted Buddha throughout his teaching career
cards.famous_story: In divine form, Mara attempted to dissuade Buddha from teaching, claiming none would understand the profound Dharma. Buddha rejected this counsel of despair.
